To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a novel hybrid framework that couples a physics based multiscaled non local approach with data driven clustering algorithms to detect coarse scale compartments in space and to model multiphase flow in such compartmentalized reservoir systems.

a hybrid clustering based multiscale approach can be used to automatically detect coarse scale compartments in a compartmentalized reservoir and to provide a physics based multiscaled modeling framework.

1) A hybrid framework for an automatic detection and representation of coarse scale compartments in a compartmentalized reservoir is presented, in order to provide a fast, yet physically accurate modeling approach; 2) A non local formulation for multiphase flow in porous media, in which the flow is described as a function of phase potential differences, is presented; 3) The proposed framework is applied to a large scale field study with a couple of hundred wells and more than 40 year production history
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing new and rigorous methods for automatic and rapid detection of distinct compartments and their dynamic properties, and using these compartments to build a physics based multiscaled reservoir model for history matching and forecasting.
developing and testing a novel and rigorous framework for a fast, yet robust and accurate multiscale reservoir analysis.
the development of a hybrid framework for a fast and accurate modeling of compartmental reservoirs, which can provide a robust and efficient framework for the reservoir management and optimization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we present a hybrid approach for multiscale reservoir modeling that combines physics based non local formulation with a rigorous data driven clustering framework for automatic detection of reservoir compartments.
the proposed framework provides a fast, accurate, and interpretable multiscale modeling framework for compartmentalized reservoir modeling and analysis.
we have presented a hybrid workflow in which we couple physics based modeling with data driven clustering for a rapid multiscale modeling of complex reservoirs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a novel hybrid framework for automatic detection of compartments and a fast, yet rigorous, multiscale modeling of the reservoir.
we have presented a hybrid framework for an automatic and fast detection of clusters in the reservoir, which can be used for multiscale modeling and history matching applications.

the presented hybrid framework can be applied to a wide range of reservoir studies applications including history matching, reservoir modeling, uncertainty quantification, and field development planning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a physics based modeling framework can be used in conjunction with clustering techniques to provide an efficient workflow for reservoir analysis and forecasting.
the proposed framework is able to provide a fast, yet reliable and robust workflow that can be applied to a wide range of applications in reservoir analysis and production optimization.
a fast, yet robust and accurate non local formulation can provide an excellent alternative to conventional numerical methods, especially in cases where the number of compartments is large.
